This Criminal Revision Petition is filed by the  petitioner/accused No.1, being aggrieved by the order  dated 29.07.2022 in Spl.C.C.No.134/2020 on the file of  XLVII Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge for CBI  Cases, Bengaluru (CCH-48), wherein the application filed  under Section 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for  short 'Cr.P.C.,') seeking to discharge the petitioner for  the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of  the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and under Section  9 of Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in  Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (for short 'KPIDFE  Act').

3.

Thereafter, the  complainant said to have invested a total amount of  Rs.7,00,000/- to the Company on different occasions.
5. The petitioner had to give the dividend in the month of  January 2018.
The complainant had called to the office  on several occasions, however, they did not receive the  call.
On 10.01.2018, around 11 'O' clock in the morning  when the complainant went near the office, many people  were gathering in front of the office.
On enquiry, the  complainant learnt that the petitioner had closed his  office and escaped from Bengaluru.
Immediately, he  lodged a complaint before the jurisdictional police.

The  jurisdictional police after conducting the investigation,
 submitted the charge sheet.

the  respondent - State.

Further, the investigating officer dropped Sections 4, 5  and 6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Scheme  (Banning) Act and Section 9 of K.P.I.D.F.E Act on the  ground that there is no material to invoke the said  provision against the accused.

8. It is further submitted that the petitioner is not  connected to the company either directly or indirectly,
 however, the respondent police dragged him into the  case only in order to harass the petitioner.
In fact, the  Company stands in the name of CW.9 - Usman Chand  -5-  CRL.RP No. 1196 of 2022  Pasha and the rent agreement of the Company also  stands in the name of Sheik Shameer.

9. It is further submitted that the entire reading of the  averments of the complaint and also the charge sheet, it  can be inferred that the petitioner is not related to the  Company or its day-to-day affairs.

Therefore, the  application for discharge has to be allowed by setting  aside the order dated 29.07.2022 passed by the Trial Wajid Sheikh @ Sheikh Sameer vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/433441/

sentences.text: Making such submissions, the learned counsel for  the petitioner
prays to allow the petition.
10. Per contra, the learned HCGP for the respondent - State  vehemently opposed the said contention and stated that
the petitioner had induced the public at large to invest in
the Company where he was working as a Managing  Director
. The petitioner and others had the intention to  cheat the public at large from the day when they opened  the office and offered the public to invest the money.
Therefore, there are ingredients which would attract the  provisions of the Indian Penal Code.

In addition to that,
 the Provision under Section of the K.P.I.D.F.E., Act also  attracted against the petitioner as he had cheated the  investors without returning the invested money.
-6-  CRL.RP No. 1196 of 2022
Therefore, the Trial Court rightly rejected the application  filed for discharge.
Hence, the petition deserves to be  dismissed.
Making such submissions, the learned HCGP  for the respondent-State prays to dismiss the petition.

11. After having heard the learned counsel for the respective  parties and also perused the averments of the charge  sheet, it appears that there are several investors having  invested in the Company after having spoken with the  petitioner.

Though the Company is not standing in his  name, many employees of the Company have made their Wajid Sheikh @ Sheikh Sameer vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/433441/
5  statements before the police stating that the petitioner  was instrumental in forming the said Company and also  he was attending to the investors and he was giving  instructions to the customers to deposit in various  schemes.

12. Now, it is relevant to refer to Section 9 of the  K.P.I.D.F.E., Act, which reads thus:
 "9. Fraudulent default by Financial  Establishment.- Any Financial Establishment,
 which fraudulently defaults any repayment of  deposit on maturity along with any benefit in  the form of interest, bonus, profit or in any  other form as promised or fraudulently fails to  -7-  CRL.RP No. 1196 of 2022 render service as assured against the deposit,
every person including the promoter, director,
partner, manager or any other person or an employee responsible for the management or conducting of the business or affairs of such Financial Establishment, shall on conviction,
be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six years and with fine which may extend to one lakh of rupees and such Financial Establishment also shall be liable for a fine which may extend to an amount equivalent to five lakhs of rupees, or where such deposits is quantifiable in terms of money twice the amount involved in such default whichever is more;

Provided that in the absence of special and adequate reasons recorded by the Special Court in the judgment of the Court, the imprisonment shall not be less than three years and the fine shall not be less than twenty thousand rupees as against each individual and not less than one lakh of rupees against such Financial Establishment.

Explanation.- For the purpose of this section a Financial Establishment, which commits default in repayment of such deposit with such Wajid Sheikh @ Sheikh Sameer vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/433441/
6 benefits in form of interest, bonus, profit or in any other form as promised or fails to render any specific service promised against such deposit, or fails to render any specific service

-8-  CRL.RP No. 1196 of 2022  agreed against the deposit with an intention of  causing wrongful gain to one person or  wrongful loss to another person or commits  such defaults due to its inability arising out of  impracticable or commercially not viable  promises made while accepting such deposit  or arising out of deployment of money or  assets acquired out of the deposits in such  manner as it involves inherent risk in  recovering the same when needed shall, be  deemed to have committed a default or failed  to render the specific service, fraudulently.
13.

On reading of the above said Provision, it makes it clear  that every person including promoter, director or partner  and manager or any other person responsible for the  management of the business or financial establishment is  also held liable for the offences.
In addition to that, one  of the employees of the Company, namely, Srinivas
had  given his statement, stating that the petitioner was  working as the proprietor of the said firm.

Therefore,
 the involvement of the petitioner in the affairs and  business of the Company stands established at this  stage.
It is a settled principle of law that at the time of framing  the charge, the Court has to see prima-facie material  placed before it.

A detailed enquiry of the offence is not Wajid Sheikh @ Sheikh Sameer vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/433441/
7  required at the time of framing of the charge.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. On careful reading of the averments of the charge sheet  and also the complaint, I am of the considered opinion  that the order passed by the Trial Court appears to be  appropriate and there is no infirmity in the said order.
Hence, I declined to interfere in the said findings.

Therefore, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition stands dismissed.
